candidate.title: unifieddb: add concurrent projection shadow-load gate

leading_hypothesis: The lease-fenced UnifiedDB-to-ClayGraph projection worker can preserve authoritative write availability through derived backlog and a crashed-worker live-lease interval while keeping consequential graph use fail-closed until exact-current recovery.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The observed pass is an artifact of a single-host disposable workload and pressure thresholds; under concurrent production the projection may either block authoritative writes, permit stale graph use, fail lease takeover, or hide contention/tail-latency failures.

claim_boundary: single-host disposable target-VPS shadow load only
does not prove production migration or systemd service activation
does not prove multi-host lease safety
does not prove power-loss or kernel-panic durability
does not prove 24h operating window or whole Frank v0.1 acceptance

live_external_refresh.finding: SQLite 3.53.4 is the current 2026-07-24 release and its official release lineage includes the WAL-reset corruption fix. SQLite documents the WAL-reset race as affecting versions through 3.51.2 under concurrent WAL writer/checkpoint conditions; fixed releases begin at 3.51.3 and later.
live_external_refresh.architecture_effect: Keep the exact hash-pinned fixed SQLite runtime lane; do not treat the target system SQLite 3.45.1 as release-safe for concurrent Frank WAL state.
